aggressive_definition_excerpt: Plasma isoflavone levels were not statistically significantly associated with the risk of advanced prostate cancer.
study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study.
reason: The abstract analyzes total incident prostate cancer and separately reports an analysis of advanced incident prostate cancer. It also reports localized disease, which is nonaggressive. The 14,203 men describe the underlying prospective cohort, while the total nested case-control analytic sample is not stated directly.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: These inverse associations were strengthened after analysis was confined to localized cases, with ORs in the highest group of plasma genistein and equol compared with the lowest of 0.54 (95% CI, 0.29 to 1.01; P(trend) = .03) and 0.43 (95% CI, 0.22 to 0.82; P(trend) = .02), respectively.
estimate_classifications.reason: The genistein estimate is explicitly for localized prostate cancer, a nonaggressive endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Although plasma daidzein showed no association, the highest tertile for plasma equol, a metabolite of daidzein, was significantly associated with a decreased risk of total prostate cancer (OR = 0.60; 95% CI, 0.36 to 0.99; P(trend) = .04).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is explicitly for total incident prostate cancer. Although the displayed exposure is labeled soy, the measured exposure in the abstract is plasma equol.

additional_estimates.comparison: Plasma isoflavone levels; contrast not specified for advanced disease in the abstract
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Plasma isoflavone levels were not statistically significantly associated with the risk of advanced prostate cancer.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
